name: agent-builder-optional-release-agent
body:
The distributed agent-builder agent template opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md (product source embedded into the apg binary via include_str! and installed by apg init into ~/.config/opencode/agents/) scaffolds an OPTIONAL, per-repo release-agent that fills the slot the optional coordinator is absent from. Unlike the distributed suite agents, the release-agent is GENERATED per repo, distributed nowhere: it carries repo-specific release-artefact write grants and the repo's remote/branch conventions, interviewed per repo exactly like the build gates.

Its shape: mode: subagent, hidden: true, generated: true; zero question (it routes questions through the coordinator); it actions zero Feedback — it returns an ACTIONED/WONT-FIX claim like every generated agent. It is grant-unusual in exactly one way: it is the ONLY generated agent granted git push * and git tag *, and its grant is ask — each push/tag command prompts for explicit human approval. Every OTHER generated agent gets zero push/tag grant (denied by deny-by-default).

Release-artefact write scope (per requirements.requirement.code-writer-worktree-only-writes): releases run from MAIN, so the release-agent's write grants target the MAIN checkout — it is one of the two agent carve-outs of global.constraint.worktree-isolation and carries zero apg/.worktrees/*/ mirror. Its main-write set is REPO-SPECIFIC and free of a fixed list: the agent-builder ANALYSES the repo (what its release touches — e.g. version files, packaging formulae, changelog, release scripts) and RECOMMENDS the set, confirmed through the coordinator interview exactly like build gates and test tiers. The spec fixes this policy alone; zero release-artefact path list is a law.

The release-agent performs the repo's release: it is granted the release-adjacent git ops (tagging and pushing the branch and tags) plus write access to that per-repo release-artefact set on main. The codebase-navigator dispatches it through the `subagent` tool ONLY after obtaining explicit user consent, and the grant is ask, so approval surfaces both at dispatch and per command.

This is a deliberate CARVE-OUT of the law "push/tag are human-approved acts" (requirements.requirement.push-tag-human-approved-release-only; the scoped law is requirements.constraint.push-tag-release-agent-carve-out): the rule binds every other agent and path, while the release-agent alone is exempt, and only behind the consent gate and the per-op ask.

The carve-out is an AGENT-policy statement, external to a binary one. The apg binary pushes and tags nowhere: it is git2-only (default-features = false; the git CLI is unused) and scripts/release.sh pushes nothing — the release-agent may run it and then push/tag itself. The wording of that binary-policy statement on the binary-doc surfaces reads human-approved acts, per requirements.requirement.push-tag-human-approved-release-only.

Surfaces to edit (all real docs File nodes in the branch graph):
- opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md — the optional release-agent in the generated set (roster intro, ### release-agent (optional) section, workflow interview bullet, step-4/step-5 scaffold) and its grant shape (push/tag ask; main-checkout release-artefact edits derived per repo by analysis + interview; zero worktree mirror); push/tag prose states ONLY the release-agent is granted push/tag, as ask.
- opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md — explicit user consent BEFORE dispatching the release-agent; release-agent named by the navigator's `subagent`-action rule (resource = the target agent ID); human-approved push/tag phrasing.
- AGENTS.md — the optional release-agent, the consent gate, the release-agent-only push/tag rule, its per-repo main-write scope, and the human-approved phrasing.

Acceptance criteria:
- opencode-suite/agents/agent-builder.md offers and scaffolds the optional per-repo release-agent: mode: subagent, hidden: true, generated: true, zero question, returning ACTIONED/WONT-FIX claims; it is the ONLY generated agent granted push/tag, as ask; every other generated agent carries zero push/tag grant.
- The template instructs the agent-builder to derive the release-agent's main-checkout write set by analysing the repo and to confirm it via the coordinator interview; it hardcodes zero release-artefact path list as a rule, and grants zero worktree mirror for it.
- opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md states the navigator obtains explicit user consent BEFORE dispatching the release-agent, and its `subagent`-action rule names release-agent as a dispatch target.
- AGENTS.md documents the release-agent, the consent gate, the release-agent-only push/tag rule, its per-repo main-write scope and the human-approved phrasing.
- The binary is git2-only and pushes and tags nowhere.
- Scope is product source + the repo guide alone; the repo's own .opencode/agents/** are consumer artifacts and are untouched.
